one_month_reasoning: AMAT's own FQ4 report is 2026-11-12 after the close, outside the window. Inside the window are value-chain prints that move semicap as a group: Micron FQ4 on 2026-09-30 after the close (not yet out when this was written; prior guide was FY27 capex above the mid-$40B range vs ~$27B in FY26, with every FY27 quarter above the ~$10B FQ4 level), Samsung Q3 preliminary results (~Oct 7), ASML Q3 (Oct 14), TSMC Q3 and first 2027 capex color (~Oct 15), Lam Research (Oct 21), Intel (~Oct 22), SK hynix and hyperscaler capex (late Oct); KLA may land at or just after the window's end. Customer capex signals will very likely be positive, but the June-September drawdown (closing high $723.00 on 6/30 to a $415.38 close on 9/16) was driven by AI-capex-durability sentiment, not chain data, and the stock has since rebounded +23% to $512, so momentum and reversal roughly cancel. The BIS Affiliates Rule suspension's nominal end (2026-11-09) and its reported extension to 2027-01-10 both fall outside the window. Net: essentially symmetric around spot at ~16-17% one-month vol (60%/3.5), with a very slight positive tilt from likely-strong capex prints. Unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E on FY2028E (NTM at horizon) EPS $23.5 x 22x plus ~$8/sh net cash (= $525, weight 0.6) and FY2027E EPS $19.5 x 25x plus net cash (= $496, weight 0.4) = ~$513, rounded to $515. EPS is now anchored on consensus (FY27 $18.43, FY28 $23.85) and SEMI's corrected WFE path (+21.8% 2027, +14.1% 2028); the multiple is still below today's ~27.7x on FY27 because late-cycle semicap de-rates ahead of decelerating growth.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY28 EPS $23.85 on $55.5B revenue (MarketScreener, 2026-09-29) haircut ~1.5% for late-cycle revision risk. Smaller haircut than the supervisor's 6% because the corrected SEMI path is stronger than the one I used in round 1.

Morgan Stanley moved its multiple from 26x to 22x on 2026-09-28 (single note, secondary access); Lam trades at similar forward multiples. Raised from 21x in round 1: SEMI's corrected path still has +14% WFE growth in 2028, so in Sep-2027 the market will not yet be pricing a 2028 decline, but some de-rating from ~27.7x FY27 today is appropriate for a late-cycle peak-margin setup.

Cash+investments $14.50B less debt $6.54B = $7.96B ($10.0/sh on 793.6M shares); $2.42B of that is strategic equity stakes, which I count at roughly half, giving ~$8/sh on ~790M diluted shares at the horizon (buybacks slowed to $1.14B over 9M). bear.story: AI-capex durability doubts become real: hyperscaler/AI-lab funding stress (the Aug 19 trigger) leads to 2028 capex cuts; memory pricing at ~86% gross margins (Micron) rolls over in 2027 and memory makers slow tool orders; China (28% of revenue) is hit when the BIS Affiliates Rule returns after its suspension lapses (nominally 2026-11-09, reportedly extended to 2027-01-10) or by domestic substitution. Market prices a 2028 WFE decline: ~$20-21 NTM EPS at ~15x.

base.story: WFE grows ~22% in 2027 as SEMI's July forecast has it (DRAM, leading-edge foundry/logic and advanced packaging carrying most of the growth, all AMAT strengths); AMAT prints ~$19-20 FY27 EPS and the market pays ~22-23x a ~$23.5 FY28 NTM EPS as growth decelerates to ~14% in 2028.

bull.story: TSMC 2027 capex well above its 2026 $60-64B, Micron FY27 capex above $45B, Korean memory fabs accelerate; WFE 2027 +25-30% (sell-side range), estimates drift to $26+ FY28 EPS and the stock exceeds the June closing high ($723) at ~28-30x.

thesis_break_reason: A close near $340 (~34% below spot, ~18x FY27 consensus $18.4 and ~14-15x a ~$23.5 FY28 NTM EPS) would sit ~18% below the $415.38 September closing low that came on sentiment alone. At that level the market would be pricing an actual 2027-28 WFE downturn: customer capex cuts at the TSMC/Micron/Samsung prints, an AMAT guide-down in Nov or Feb, or the BIS Affiliates Rule returning alongside broader China restrictions, not ordinary 60%-vol swings.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor showed that my SEMI growth figures were mis-transcribed; I re-fetched SEMI's July 14, 2026 mid-year release (Yahoo syndication) and confirmed WFE $143.9B in 2026 (+23.1%), ~$175B in 2027 (+21.8%) and ~$200B in 2028 (+14.1%), with DRAM equipment rising to $56.9B and foundry/logic to $104.7B by 2028. That is a stronger 2027 and a slightly stronger 2028 than I had, which removes part of my reason for a 21x multiple (in Sep-2027 the market should still see double-digit WFE growth ahead), so I raise the forward multiple to 22x. I now anchor EPS on consensus (FY27 $18.43, FY28 $23.85 per MarketScreener) with a small 1.5% haircut, and move my FY27 estimate to $19.5 (explicitly above consensus on the WFE path). Net cash drops from ~$10 to ~$8/share after partly discounting $2.42B of strategic equity stakes. Fair value moves from $510 to ~$515, essentially spot. Other industry evidence is unchanged: Lam's 'extraordinary' 2027 setup with 8-10 new fabs and DRAM leading; TSMC 2026 capex $60-64B; Micron FY27 capex above mid-$40B (FQ4 print tonight, not yet out); memory makers sold out for 2027. I drop the UBS $85-90B TSMC 2027 capex figure as a number (Substack-only, discounted by the supervisor) and keep it as context. I add the BIS Affiliates Rule as a dated China risk: the Federal Register suspension runs to 2026-11-09 and a Sep-28 report says it is extended to 2027-01-10 (single secondary source, so treated as reported). Net: median raised from ~$530 to ~$542 (estimate momentum plus the corrected WFE path), lognormal spread ~46% (below the 60% trailing realized, which was inflated by the +150% run and 30% drawdown), left tail fattened modestly for a memory/AI-capex bust and the China policy binary. Scenario mean ~$557. I do not adopt the supervisor's 6% FY28 haircut because the corrected SEMI path supports consensus; I agree with its ~$8 net cash and the fact corrections. Research limited to three follow-up queries for speed.
